singleSourced.context:
Expect the likes of Natural Wonders to appear in their correct locations too, although Firaxis notes that different ones will be spawned each game to "keep things fresh even on a familiar map."

Patch 1.5.0 also updates two more maps using the team's new 'Voronoi map generation' algorithm, which is designed to create more varied, natural-feeling layouts.

singleSourced.key: without joining your allies misguided wars
singleSourced.value: without joining your allies' misguided wars.
singleSourced.context: Diplomacy updates will let you use Influence to stay in an alliance "without joining your allies' misguided wars." Map loading and generation has been sped up, with more varied resource placement, and you can also expect improved plot tooltips, settlement banners, and game setup, along with a tile ruler to aid city planning.

singleSourced.value: the historic space race and deploying missions across the solar system.
singleSourced.context: This is themed around "the historic space race and deploying missions across the solar system." Don't expect to go full Civilization: Beyond Earth, perhaps, although that doesn't mean the new gameplay included in Earthrise is limited to the endgame.

singleSourced.key: chart the night sky and name the celestial bodies above
singleSourced.value: chart the night sky and name the celestial bodies above.
singleSourced.context: Humanity's interest in the stars can begin in the Antiquity or Exploration Ages, where you're able to "chart the night sky and name the celestial bodies above." Once you reach the Modern Age, you'll gain the ability to launch "early orbital missions around Earth and the Moon," and then the true space race begins in the Atomic Age.
Set up your own national space agency, launch missions across the stars, and discover "planetary features and untapped resources" that can feed back into bolstering your civ's power back home.

"This is all just a brief glimpse of the plans we have in store," Creative Director Ed Beach concludes.
